name: wazap-mcp

tools.name: learn
tools.description: The guide to these tools: ids, account_id with several accounts, the workflows, the message shape and what to do about each error code. Read it once, before the other tools; it never touches WhatsApp.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Whether the account works: status (connected, not_linked, linking with its pairing code…), sync, how fresh the history is, webhook delivery, versions. accounts lists every account, with default. Call it on NOT_CONNECTED, NOT_LINKED or SYNC_IN_PROGRESS.

include_picture.description: Add picture_url, the account's own profile photo (the link expires)

tools.name: link_account
tools.description: Pair wazap with the user's WhatsApp when get_status says not_linked, logged_out, session_corrupt or auth_failure. Show the user the code it returns: WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead. Then poll get_status every 10 s until connected.

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: Conversations, most recently active first: chat_id, name, type, unread count, last message, and whether archived, pinned, muted or left. Use it to find a chat_id.

include_pictures.description: Add picture_url, each chat's profile photo (links expire)

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read one chat, oldest to newest: the latest messages, or older ones with before (wazap asks the phone when the local history runs out). chat_id "status" reads the stories people posted, newest first, from the last hours (at most a day); they show nowhere else.

chat_id.description: Chat id from another tool, a phone number, or "status" for stories

types.description: Only these types; limit counts them, so ["call"] gives that many calls

include_previews.description: Attach a small image of each photo, up to 12

hours.description: "status" only: how far back, 24 by default

tools.name: catch_up
tools.description: What the user missed, all accounts, within budget_tokens: waiting (every open ask of 14 days, whatever the window), mentions, calls, people, groups, stories. account_id narrows it to one account; get_status names them. The mark moves first; a lost answer is since: "previous". more.cursor: the rest.

since.description: "last" (default); "previous" repeats that catch-up; or an ISO date or time from the last 14 days

hours.description: The last N hours instead; never moves the mark

include.description: Only these sections; the mark then stays

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Keep what the user says about someone, locally, never on WhatsApp: a note, tags, details find_contact matches ({"relatie": "mama"}), or handled: true for an ask dealt with elsewhere. #private keeps their words out of what you did not ask about them by name; #no-catchup keeps them out of catch_up.

chat_id.description: Chat id, or a phone number

handled.description: Off catch_up's waiting until they write again

tools.name: wait_for_messages
tools.description: Wait for messages from other people, up to timeout_seconds, and return them with a cursor: pass it to the next call so nothing that lands between calls is missed. addressed_to_me wakes only for direct messages, mentions and replies to the user. For agents that stay on the line.

chat_id.description: Chat id, or a phone number

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find messages by meaning and by words at once, in every chat or one: a paraphrase still hits; another language seldom does, so ask in the chat's language. match: "words" for exact words (a number, a URL). since, until and from narrow it; coverage and freshness say how much history was searched.

chat_id.description: Chat id, or a phone number

from.description: "me", a number, an id, or a name only one person has

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: One message in full: the message it quotes, each reaction with who left it, poll votes and event answers by person, its media, and on the user's own messages who it reached and who read it. Without account_id the id is looked for on every account.

tools.name: find_contact
tools.description: Who a name, nickname, relationship ("mama"), group, number or id means, before drafting. resolved: contact.chat_id, with number, note, tags, details and, in a write session, context. ambiguous or not_found: ask the user; never send to a guess. A name on several accounts: see fix. tag: its people.

name.description: What the user calls them ("Ana", "mamei", "fotbal"), or a number or id

qualifier.description: Tells two apart: "contabilitate", a group, the last 4 digits

tag.description: List everyone filed under this tag instead

limit.description: Ambiguous: at most 5 per account; a tag list: up to 50

include_context.description: Recent messages and the user's style, when resolved in a write session

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: The phone's address book on one account, a page at a time: saved name, phone (E.164), chat_id, contact_id, and when the last direct message was and its direction. No message words; #private people left out. address_book_synced false: not arrived yet.

order.description: recent: latest direct chat first, then the rest in address book order

tools.name: get_group_info
tools.description: A group's name, description, owner and participants (up to 500), whether the account is admin, its settings (info_locked, member_add_mode, join_approval, disappearing_seconds), its community, and the invite link for an admin. Call it before manage_group.

tools.name: get_media
tools.description: What a message's media holds: a voice note or audio as its transcript (kept once made; an API provider bills it), or with save_to its file; a photo attached as an image; any file saved at path on the machine running wazap; a copy kept on arrival answers first. MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE: gone, none kept.

save_to.description: Absolute directory; default <data-dir>/media. A recording: its file, and no new transcript

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Drafts text, media, polls, locations, forwards; sends nothing. Call it as soon as you have recipient and text: it returns draft_id and preview (recipient, number, exact text). Show that preview; confirm_send only on a yes to this text and recipient — a send in the same request is that yes.

chat_id.description: Chat id, or a phone number

text.description: The message, or the caption, poll question or place name; "" for a forward, a voice note or audio

mention_ids.description: Chat ids to @-mention; write @<number> in text for each

file_path.description: Media: absolute path on the machine running wazap

as.description: Media: a plain document, a voice note, a looping GIF

send_at.description: Send later: "2026-10-12T09:00" in time_zone, or with an offset; 1 minute to 365 days ahead

time_zone.description: IANA zone for send_at, e.g. "Europe/Bucharest"; the server's by default

tools.name: edit_message
tools.description: Replace the text of a message the linked account sent. WhatsApp allows it for 15 minutes after sending; later, send a correction instead.

tools.name: react_to_message
tools.description: React to a message with one emoji, or pass "" to take your reaction off.

tools.name: confirm_send
tools.description: Send a draft the user approved — this text, this recipient: the only call that sends, once per draft. A yes about something else: show the preview again and ask. Expired, missing or stale: draft again, show the new preview, ask again. SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: read_messages, never redo it unasked.

draft_id.description: From send_message; one with send_at is scheduled, not sent

tools.name: delete_message
tools.description: Delete a message; confirm with the user first. for_everyone: true retracts it for everyone within 2 days: the account's own message, or anyone's in a group where it is admin. for_everyone: false removes any message from the linked account's devices only.

tools.name: manage_chat
tools.description: Change a chat on WhatsApp at once, with no draft: archive, pin, mute, mark_read or mark_unread; pin_message (for everyone) or star_message on a message_id; clear or delete it for the linked account; block a person. Say what will change and wait for a yes.

chat_id.description: Chat id, or a phone number

message_id.description: pin_message, star_message and their undo; in chat_id

tools.name: manage_group
tools.description: Create a group, join one from an invite (preview first, then confirm: true), or administer one: members, name, description, photo, invite link, join requests, settings, leave. Most actions need admin. Every change shows to all members at once: say what will change, wait for a yes.

group_id.description: "<id>@g.us"; every action but create and join

participant_ids.description: create, add, remove, promote, demote, approve or reject

value.description: The name (create, set_subject) or description; "on"/"off"; set_add_mode "admins"/"all"; set_disappearing "off"/"24h"/"7d"/"90d"

file_path.description: set_picture: local JPEG, PNG or WebP

invite.description: join: a chat.whatsapp.com link or its code

confirm.description: join: true joins, after the user said yes to the preview

tools.name: scheduled_messages
tools.description: The account's scheduled messages: list (waiting ones soonest first, then the week's sent, missed, failed and cancelled ones) or cancel one by schedule_id before it goes. To schedule one, send_message with send_at, then confirm_send. Tell the user about every missed or failed one.

schedule_id.description: cancel: from the list or confirm_send

include_closed.description: list: the week's sent, missed, failed and cancelled ones too

tools.name: reminder
tools.description: The user's reminders about a chat, kept locally and posted to their webhook when due: create (chat_id, note, after_hours or due_at); condition "no_reply" fires only if nobody wrote there since ("if Ana has not answered in 2 days"). list, cancel. Nothing goes to WhatsApp.

chat_id.description: create: the chat it is about

note.description: create: what to remind the user of

after_hours.description: create: due this many hours from now

due_at.description: create: due then, "2026-10-14T09:00" in time_zone, or with an offset

time_zone.description: IANA zone for due_at; the server's by default

condition.description: no_reply: skipped if someone wrote in the chat after it was set

include_closed.description: list: the week's fired, skipped and cancelled ones too

instructions:
Call `learn` first: it returns every tool, the id formats and every error code with what to do about it. With several WhatsApp accounts, `get_status` lists them and every tool takes `account_id`: without it, a chat or message only one account knows picks that account, `catch_up` and `find_contact` cover them all, other reads use the default, and a write to a chat no account knows fails AMBIGUOUS_ACCOUNT. An agent that should act as messages arrive calls `wait_for_messages` in a loop with the cursor it returns, instead of polling.

The workflows behind these tools:
- **wazap-setup**: Install, link or repair the WhatsApp connection. Use when the user wants to connect WhatsApp to Claude, when a WhatsApp tool returns NOT_LINKED, SESSION_EXPIRED or SESSION_CORRUPT, when `get_status` is anything but connected, or when the user asks how wazap works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code or HTTP.
- **whatsapp-groups**: Catch up on a busy WhatsApp group. Use when the user asks what happened in a group, what was decided, what they are being asked to do there, or for a summary of a thread with many messages.
- **whatsapp-inbox**: Triage the user's WhatsApp. Use when they ask what they missed, what's unread, who is waiting on a reply, what needs attention today, or whom they forgot to answer.
- **whatsapp-recall**: Find something in the user's WhatsApp history. Use when they ask for an address, invoice, photo, document, link, phone number, date or a thing someone said or sent, or "what did X say about Y".
- **whatsapp-send**: Send, reply, forward, share a file or a location, react, create a poll, or change a group's photo on WhatsApp on the user's behalf. Use for any request that results in an outgoing WhatsApp message or a change others see.

Each one is available in full as the MCP prompt of the same name. Never send without the user's yes to this text and this recipient: draft with send_message (it sends nothing) and show the preview it returns. A send asked in the same request that gave the text is that yes: confirm_send it, do not ask again. A yes about something else, or one that comes after the talk moved on, is not: show the preview again and ask.
